title: Evaluation-defined internal-Hom comparison for a composite monoidal functor
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category], each with specified internal Hom $H$ and natural adjunction bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(A\otimes T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,H(A,B))$. Denote the corresponding evaluation by $\operatorname{ev}_{A,B}:A\otimes H(A,B)\to B$. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be strong monoidal functors [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] with tensorators $\mu^V_{A,B}:VA\otimes VB\to V(A\otimes B)$. For $V=F,G,GF$, define
$$c^V_{A,B}:VH(A,B)\longrightarrow H(VA,VB)$$
to be the tensor-Hom transpose of $V(\operatorname{ev}_{A,B})\circ\mu^V_{A,H(A,B)}$, using the composite tensorator $\mu^{GF}=G(\mu^F)\circ\mu^G$. Then for every $A,B\in\mathcal C$ the actual comparison maps satisfy
$$c^{GF}_{A,B}=c^G_{FA,FB}\circ G(c^F_{A,B}).$$
The tensor-Hom comparison here is defined by this evaluation transpose; no invertibility of any $c^V$ is assumed.
